summary.intent: Complete phases 42 (API unpin integrity), 43 (FUSE write durability), and 44 (IPNS conflict handling) of the CipherBox v1.1 milestone using the GSD workflow manager — discuss, plan, and execute all three gap-closure phases sourced from UAT audit PR #484.
summary.outcome: Phases 42 and 43 fully executed and verified (8 plans each across multiple waves, all tests green, code reviews and verification artifacts committed); Phase 44 discussed and planned (5 plans committed) but not yet executed. Key security fix shipped: cross-tenant unpin attack surface closed with guardedUnpin advisory lock + transactional outbox.

repo: The IPFS unpin endpoint (POST /ipfs/unpin) was protected only by JwtAuthGuard with no ownership check — any account holder could destroy another user's pinned content using a harvested CID

Kubo v0.40 runs with the 'server' profile and swarm port 4001 publicly exposed: the server profile only disables local-network peer discovery, NOT public DHT participation — all pinned CIDs are broadcast as provider records to DHT crawlers, making CIDs non-private identifiers even though blobs are encrypted
The writable-share save path drops prunedCids without calling unpin — no legitimate cross-user unpin flow exists anywhere in the codebase, making every no-row unpin either a benign race or an attack
BYO-IPFS unpin is broken in both directions today; the new server-side guardedUnpin semantics fix the server side for free ('not pinned' gets swallowed without error)

pnpm/jest flag forwarding is broken: `pnpm --filter @pkg test -- --testPathPattern=X` fails because pnpm inserts a bare `--` that jest treats as a positional regex argument; correct invocation is `pnpm --filter @pkg exec jest --testPathPattern='X'`
gsd commit helper returns `"committed": false` as a false negative even when the commit landed — always verify with `git log`, never blind-retry on that signal
No .prettierignore existed — prettier was silently reformatting .planning/ docs and breaking markdown table syntax (e.g., regex pipes in VALIDATION.md rendered as table column separators)

The gsd cleanup-wave helper is not idempotent: already-merged entries report `branch_mismatch` on a second run and abort the whole batch — write a reduced manifest with only remaining un-merged entries when re-running after a partial failure
Running worktree.cleanup-wave from inside an agent worktree directory causes false `base_mismatch` errors because the helper resolves repoRoot from cwd — must always be run from the repo root
Decision coverage gate uses mechanical grep for literal `D-NN:` citation tokens in plan must_haves sections — prose references without the ID token fail the gate

code.finding: Writable-share saves drop prunedCids without calling unpin — no legitimate cross-user unpin path exists through this route; identified as a separate deferred concern from Phase 42 scope

handle_release journal ordering enforced by plan 43-02: journal.put(844) → handle.cleanup(892) → reply.ok(894) → spawn(904) → journal.remove-on-success(943); this ordering ensures fsync barrier before OS ack (D-04/D-05)

Upload compensation path fired a global pin/rm on the CID — a content-addressed dedup hazard when the same CID is shared across users; rerouted through guardedUnpin in plan 42-05 with a D-13 race window comment

CR-08 alignment bug: Windows UploadSpawnParams was calling journal.remove on upload success before per-file IPNS publish succeeded, creating the exact orphan window the POSIX path was designed to eliminate; caught by post-execution re-verifier and fixed inline
Kubo swarm port 4001 is publicly exposed (tcp+udp) with server profile active — all pinned CIDs are visible to public DHT crawlers; blobs are encrypted but CIDs are public identifiers by design

guardedUnpin added: pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(cid)) → row delete + refcount within one transaction → if last reference insert pending_unpins → commit → best-effort Kubo pin/rm post-commit; closes concurrent-delete race on deduped CIDs
Unpin errors swallowed with .catch(logger.warn) — no current web caller reads the unpin response status, confirming that the opaque {success:true} DTO decision (D-11) is safe without breaking changes

workflow: GSD execute-phase worktrees are isolated on a base SHA — `nest build` and `cargo build` side-effects (e.g., openapi.json reformatting) on the main tree must be reverted with `git checkout --` before merging worktrees to avoid false conflicts
zsh multi-glob rm (`rm -rf node_modules apps/*/node_modules`) aborts entirely if any glob matches nothing — use explicit single paths to avoid silent partial cleanup
When a merge leaves MERGE_HEAD (all conflicts auto-resolved but commit step failed), `git commit --no-edit` is the correct recovery rather than aborting and re-merging

1Password SSH commit signing requires `dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true` on all git Bash calls; signing failures require the user to restart the 1Password desktop app — not recoverable in-session otherwise

Verifier gap items requiring a live runtime (FUSE mount, crash-replay cycle, tray notification) should be captured in a UAT.md artifact rather than blocking phase completion — static verification + code-review findings are sufficient to mark the automated portion passed

Answering user questions by re-presenting option menus instead of giving direct prose answers causes friction — verify uncertain claims with code checks, then answer plainly before presenting any follow-up choices

friction: 1Password SSH signing failures mid-session: required user to restart the 1Password app; `dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true` is required on all git commits but is not the default, making it easy to forget
gsd commit helper returns `committed: false` even on success — every commit required an explicit `git log` verification pass, adding latency throughout the session
cleanup-wave helper aborts on first blocked entry and is not idempotent — partial failures required writing reduced manifests with only un-merged entries before re-running
Planner agent hit a socket error mid-session after writing plans 01-03, requiring filesystem fallback (verify partial plans on disk, spawn continuation planner for 04-08)
Two session quota interruptions during Phase 43 execution waves, requiring conversation restart and re-dispatch; one interruption caused false re-dispatch of executors that were still running
User sent accidental text input ('touring wyatt web bossy') twice during live execution waves, requiring interruption handling and explicit resume confirmation
openapi.json formatting drift: `nest build` reformats the file as a side-effect, polluting worktree diffs and blocking clean merges unless explicitly reverted first
prettier was silently mangling .planning/ markdown docs (broke regex table syntax in VALIDATION.md) before .prettierignore was created — root cause took time to diagnose

Windows winfsp cross-compilation fails on macOS due to pre-existing issues in windows-future and winfsp-sys crates — no automated gate validation for Windows path changes; changes must be verified structurally only
Communication friction: assistant re-presented option menus in response to direct questions instead of answering plainly, requiring explicit user correction mid-discussion
